title: E6 five-minute planning checkpoint form A
instructions: Continue with the Student Skills Newsletter prompt about transferring one group-project habit to an outside-school problem. Make both compact-planning decisions before submitting.

parts.prompt: Which plan creates the clearest introduction–body–conclusion route for using role assignment during a neighbourhood clean-up?

options.text: Introduction: name role assignment and the clean-up. Body 1: show initial confusion and how matching people to rubbish collection, sorting and supplies created order. Body 2: show a missing volunteer and explain how reassigning one role kept the work moving. Conclusion: state how the habit made responsibility visible and adaptable.
Introduction: define neighbourhoods. Body 1: describe every school project. Body 2: list types of rubbish. Conclusion: introduce recycling laws.
Introduction: claim teamwork always succeeds. Body 1: say the clean-up was good. Body 2: repeat that it was good. Conclusion: add a new example about studying alone.
Write the complete introduction first, then decide whether the response needs an outside-school example.

choice_rationales.A: Each paragraph has a distinct job, specific evidence and an explicit link to the chosen habit.
choice_rationales.B: The route drifts into broad background and a new legal topic without explaining the transfer.
choice_rationales.C: The absolute claim, repeated body job and unrelated final example weaken task control.
choice_rationales.D: The outside-school example is a requirement that must shape the plan before drafting.

parts.hint: Protected checkpoint: no hint is available.
parts.correct_explanation: The strongest plan uses two developing body jobs and ties both the initial organisation and later adjustment to role assignment.

parts.prompt: The plan names roles and events but never explains how they solved the problem. What is the most important repair before drafting?

options.text: Add a link-back after each body example explaining how clear responsibility reduced confusion or enabled adaptation.
Add a second unrelated school habit to increase variety.
Replace the specific evidence with general statements about teamwork.
Remove the conclusion so there is more room for event details.

choice_rationales.A: The missing explanation is the connection between the chosen habit, the action and the problem solved.
choice_rationales.B: A second habit breaks the prompt's one-focus scope.
choice_rationales.C: General statements would weaken rather than explain the evidence.
choice_rationales.D: Removing closure does not repair the missing analysis in the body.

parts.hint: Protected checkpoint: no hint is available.
parts.correct_explanation: A compact plan must record not just events but the explanation linking each event to the controlling focus.
